chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Abī Ayyūb, from Abī ʿUbaydah and al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

He was asked about a man who killed a woman by mistake while she was in labor with her child. He said: “Five thousand dirhams, and upon him is the diyah of the one in her womb: a ghurrah, a male servant or a female servant, or forty dinars.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: These reports do not contradict what we presented earlier, that the diyah of the fetus is one hundred dinars, because those reports are to be understood as referring to a fetus that had become complete and full-formed, except that the spirit had not yet entered it. This report is to be understood as referring to a woman who miscarries a clot or a lump of flesh, so its diyah is a ghurrah: a male slave or a female slave. Thus there is no contradiction between them in any way, and what indicates what we have said is what he narrated:

key_terms.خَطَأً: by mistake; indicating accidental rather than intentional killing
key_terms.دِيَةُ: prescribed blood-money compensation owed for wrongful killing or injury
key_terms.غُرَّةٌ: a specified compensation, here explained as a male or female servant, for the fetus at a particular stage
key_terms.مُضْغَةً: a lump-of-flesh stage of embryonic development
key_terms.وَصِيفٌ: a male servant given as compensation
key_terms.وَصِيفَةٌ: a female servant given as compensation

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for accidentally killing a pregnant woman and her fetus in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report gives a legal ruling concerning accidental killing of a pregnant woman and the compensation owed both for the woman and for the fetus. It also preserves Shaykh al-Ṭūsī’s reconciliation between reports by distinguishing between stages of fetal development in determining the amount of diyah.
